title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.47, section 4, 'Double visage'). Take k algebraic over Q and reduce to k = Qbar. The question is whether the functor M -> (T_DR(M), T_B(M), comparison iso) is fully faithful on motives. Here T_DR carries no Hodge filtration and T_B no Hodge structure. In modern terms this is the full faithfulness of the de Rham–Betti realization.

Tannakian reformulation. Let G = Aut^tensor(T_B) on the tannakian subcategory generated by M. G is the motivic Galois group of M over Q. The comparison isomorphism gives a point g in G(C), well defined modulo G(Qbar). This is a C-point of the period torsor, trivialised by a Qbar-point. For a G-module V (V = T_B(M)), the de Rham lattice is T_DR(M) = g(Vbar), with Vbar = V tensor Qbar, inside V tensor C. Hom(1, M) corresponds to V^G. Elements of V that are 'de Rham–Betti' are those in V ∩ g(Vbar). So full faithfulness is equivalent to V^G = V ∩ g(Vbar) for every V, and one may reduce to V simple; the Tate case works.

This page.
1. Pointwise criterion. x lies in Vbar ∩ g(Vbar) iff x and y = g^{-1}x both lie in Vbar.
   - Let Tbar be the Zariski closure of g over Qbar, i.e. the smallest Qbar-subvariety of G containing g (taken modulo G(Qbar)).
   - The set {h : h^{-1}x = y} is a Qbar-subvariety containing g, so it contains Tbar. Hence t s^{-1} lies in G_x for all s, t in Tbar(C).
   - Conversely, if Tbar·Tbar^{-1} lies in G_x, then g^{-1}x = h^{-1}x for a Qbar-point h of Tbar, so g^{-1}x lies in Vbar.
   - So the condition is equivalent to Rbar ⊂ G_x, where Rbar is the closure of the image of Tbar × Tbar -> G, (s,t) -> s t^{-1}.
2. Reduction to a subgroup. Let H be the algebraic subgroup generated by R.
   - The marginal note says Tbar, Rbar, H do not depend on the representative of g in its G(Qbar)-coset; this holds with the convention s t^{-1}.
   - Then V ∩ g(Vbar) = V^H.
   - So full faithfulness is equivalent to: for every representation V of G, V^H = V^G.
3. Sufficient conditions. Grothendieck notes that H = G suffices but is not necessary. It suffices that H contain a Borel subgroup of G (G connected; cf. 'NB Connexe' on p.47). The reason: for v in V^P with P parabolic, G/P -> V, g -> gv is a map from a projective variety to an affine space, hence constant.
   - H = G is what Grothendieck's period conjecture (generic period point) gives over Qbar.
   - The weaker condition is exactly that H be an epimorphic subgroup of G.
4. Margin. He plans to test this on CM abelian varieties and elliptic curves.
5. Section 5. For k of finite type (transcendental) over Q, the naive analogue for a fixed M is called 'idiot'. One can at best hope for statements depending on the transcendence degree of a minimal field of definition (moduli). The next page passes to k algebraically closed and to the relative version over S with a connection (Gauss–Manin).
errors: Order conventions are inconsistent ('t^{-1}s' vs 's^{-1}t'). The invariance claimed in the margin, under changing g within its G(Qbar)-coset, requires the map (s,t) -> s t^{-1} with g taken modulo right multiplication by G(Qbar). This is minor.
The Borel criterion presupposes G connected, or else H must also meet every component. This is only hinted at by 'NB Connexe' on the previous page.
The step 'V ∩ g(Vbar) = V^H' needs H defined over Qbar and descent V^G tensor Qbar = Vbar^G. Both hold, but this is implicit.
The page is heavily crossed out. The final formulation ('il suffit qu'il contienne un groupe de Borel') is stated without proof, though it is correct.

ideas.what: Identify the comparison isomorphism with a point g of G(C)/G(Qbar) (period torsor point). Then T_DR = g(Vbar), and the de Rham–Betti classes in V are V ∩ g(Vbar).
ideas.modern_name: Period torsor; de Rham–Betti structures; full faithfulness of the de Rham–Betti realization
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (period conjecture, via Lang 1966 and André); developed by André (Une introduction aux motifs, 2004) and Bost–Charles (2016)
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's own texts. The conjecture is reported in Lang's 'Introduction to transcendental numbers' footnote and in André's book.

ideas.what: Reduce full faithfulness to a group-theoretic condition. Take the Zariski closure Tbar of the period point, R = Tbar·Tbar^{-1}, and H the group it generates. Then V ∩ g(Vbar) = V^H, and full faithfulness is equivalent to V^H = V^G for all representations.
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian group of the de Rham–Betti realization (G_dRB) inside the motivic Galois group; Zariski closure of the period point
ideas.usually_credited_to: André; Bost–Charles (de Rham–Betti group); implicit in the motivic Galois group literature

ideas.what: H = G is sufficient but not necessary. It suffices that H contain a Borel subgroup, i.e. that H have the same invariants as G in every representation.
ideas.modern_name: Epimorphic subgroups (parabolic subgroups are epimorphic); Deligne–Milne criterion for full faithfulness of restriction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bien–Borel (1992) for epimorphic subgroups; Deligne–Milne (1982) for tannakian criteria

ideas.what: Suggested test cases: CM abelian varieties and elliptic curves.
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic independence of periods (Chudnovsky); analytic subgroup theorem (Wüstholz); period conjecture for 1-motives (Huber–Wüstholz)

ideas.what: Over transcendental fields of finite type, naive full faithfulness for a fixed M is hopeless ('idiot'). Expect only statements controlled by the transcendence degree of the field of moduli.
ideas.modern_name: Period conjecture over function fields / transcendence degree of periods (André's generalized period conjecture)

missed.claim: In 1965 Grothendieck explicitly separates the de Rham–Betti full-faithfulness conjecture from the period conjecture. He shows the former is equivalent to an invariant-theoretic condition on the group H generated by Tbar·Tbar^{-1}, where Tbar is the Qbar-Zariski closure of the period point. He observes that density of the period point (H = G) is sufficient but not necessary, a Borel subgroup in H being enough. This is the epimorphic-subgroup criterion, decades before Bien–Borel, and an early version of the G_dRB versus G_mot comparison usually attributed to André and Bost–Charles.
missed.quote: Il suffit qu'on ait H=G, mais cette condition n'est pas nécessaire. Il suffit qu'il contienne un k-groupe de Borel de G
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents that Grothendieck himself formulated the dRB full-faithfulness conjecture as strictly weaker than the period conjecture, with an exact group-theoretic reformulation. That is relevant to the history and attribution of the period conjecture and of de Rham–Betti structures (Bost–Charles).

missed.claim: Whether the stabiliser-type group H can actually be a proper epimorphic (e.g. parabolic-containing) subgroup of the motivic Galois group is left open. For pure motives with reductive G, this would mean full faithfulness without period density.
missed.quote: mais cette condition n'est pas nécessaire
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete intermediate question between the dRB conjecture and the period conjecture. In the semisimple setting one could ask whether H is automatically reductive, which would force H = G.

deep.surprise_reason: The conjectures themselves (period conjecture, dRB full faithfulness) are attributed to Grothendieck and well studied. What is notable is the precise unpublished reduction to the group generated by the closure of the period point, and the explicit remark that only an epimorphic/Borel-containing condition is needed. A specialist would find this a nice early detail, not a new theorem.
transcription_corrections: 'l'adhérence de T_x T̄ → Ḡ' should read 'l'adhérence de l'image de T̄ × T̄ → Ḡ, (s,t) ↦ s^{-1}t'.
'Or soit R̄ l'image de R̄ dans G' likely means 'R l'image de R̄ dans G' (descent from Qbar to G).
'la relation x ∈ V∩g(V̄) équivaut' — the first V is unbarred (Q-rational V) in that inserted line.
'lien de g sur G_Q̄' is probably a remark on the class of g modulo G(Qbar) ('image de g dans G(C)/G(Q̄)'); uncertain.
Margin: 'NB T̄, R̄, H̄ ne dépendent pas du choix de g dans gG(Q̄)', i.e. the representative of the coset.
Margin: 'Regarder variétés abéliennes à multiplication complexe, courbes elliptiques'.
Last lines of section 5: 'calcul de T_B et T_DR si k est ±modulaire (p.ex. courbes), en fonction du degré de transcendance minimum'; uncertain.
